open_obligations: Identify exactly which of Anil et al.'s assumptions Proposition 7 relaxes (e.g. probabilistic labels).
Check that the adp protocol matches Anil et al.'s formulation.
Do not read this as refuting Anil et al.'s theorem within its stated assumptions.
in.other_title: Proposition 7: equilibria of the adp prover-verifier game need not be valid proofs
in.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols under their assumptions (deterministic labels, realizable complete and sound verifier, instance revealed after the verifier commits). Hammond and Adam-Day's Proposition 7 gives a probabilistic decision problem and adp game where, although a valid proof with completeness error 0 exists, being a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of prover-verifier games correspond to valid proofs once Anil et al.'s restrictions are relaxed

open_obligations: Check that worst-case losses in nip replace Anil et al.'s expected losses.
Note that approximate equilibria are allowed in Hammond et al.
Check the assumption that a valid proof system exists.
in.other_title: Theorem 8: valid interactive proofs = verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of nip
in.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols in their single-message game. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that for problems with a valid proof system a profile is a valid interactive proof iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of nip, which has alternating messages and worst-case losses.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: correspondence between verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria and valid proof protocols, extended to multi-turn interaction

open_obligations: Check that the helpful/sneaky role conditioning is the main change from Anil et al.'s game.
Note Kirchner et al. state LLM training does not meet the unrestricted prover-class assumption.
Check the two ordering conditions on prover reward (Eq. 1).
in.other_title: Verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff completeness and soundness
in.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols when the prover always argues for label 1. Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 proves the same equivalence for a game where the follower is a role-conditioned helpful or sneaky prover with their utilities RV and RP, assuming the prover class is all deterministic mappings.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium as the condition for completeness and soundness, with a role-conditioned helpful/sneaky prover

open_obligations: Compare the assumptions of Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 (Appendix A) with Anil et al.'s Theorem 2 to confirm they are strictly weaker
Check that both theorems assume a comparable prover hypothesis class (all deterministic mappings)
in.other_title: Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 restates Anil et al.'s verifier-leading PVG theorem with relaxed assumptions
in.rationale: Anil et al.'s Theorem 2 links verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria to complete and sound protocols; the authors explicitly generalize this result by relaxing its assumptions on loss and reward, which is a direct extension of a cited theorem.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Equivalence of verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria with complete and sound protocols, under weaker loss and reward assumptions

open_obligations: Check Proposition 7's proof in Appendix C.1 (p22 L42 onward) against the exact hypotheses of Anil et al.'s verifier-leading theorem
Confirm that Anil et al.'s theorem indeed assumes zero soundness error and a deterministic verifier, as the authors state at p22 L7-L10
in.other_title: Hammond et al. argue Anil et al.'s adp equilibrium-proof correspondence holds only narrowly
in.rationale: The authors do not dispute Anil et al.'s theorem under its stated assumptions but prove that the correspondence fails when those assumptions are relaxed, and say at p22 L7-L10 that its strength is severely limited by requiring zero soundness error. This is an argument that the cited result is limited, so CRITIQUES rather than CHALLENGES.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether equilibria of a one-message prover-verifier game correspond to valid interactive proofs; the critique applies when soundness error or randomised verifiers are allowed

text: The authors prove (Theorem 2) that in verifier-leading sequential PVG formulations where the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy, reaching a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is both necessary and sufficient for a desirable (complete and sound) proof-verification protocol; sufficiency follows because otherwise the verifier could do strictly better by switching to the complete and sound verifier, to which the prover would respond with correct proofs.
title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
